title: Copying and making patterns
keyIdea: A repeating pattern is one small part that comes again and again: red, blue, red, blue. That small part is called the unit of repeat. Say the pattern out loud to find it, and then you know what comes next. You can copy a pattern bead by bead, keep it going, spot a bead that breaks it, and make your own by picking a part and repeating it.

kid: Look: red, blue, red, blue. It goes again and again. That is a pattern.
Say it out loud. Red, blue, red, blue, red… what next? Blue! The red, blue part comes back each time.
Patterns can be sounds too. Clap, stamp, clap, stamp. Your hands and feet can make a pattern.
Is one bead wrong? Say it from the start. If a bead does not fit, swap it. Now make your own. Pick red and yellow. Then do it again, and again.
adult: This is early mathematics, under spatial reasoning and pattern. Development Matters for 3 and 4 year olds says children talk about and identify patterns around them, extend and create ABAB patterns such as stick, leaf, stick, leaf, and notice and correct an error in a repeating pattern. In Reception they continue, copy and create repeating patterns. The Head Start framework lists the same steps: recognise, copy, extend and create simple patterns.

The key idea is the unit of repeat, sometimes called the core: the shortest part that repeats. In red, blue, red, blue it is red, blue (an AB pattern). In clap, clap, stamp it is three long (AAB). Saying a pattern aloud with a steady beat helps children feel the unit. Spotting it early is a strong sign of later success in maths, because number patterns and counting in steps grow from it.

Common mistakes: copying only the colours you like and not the order; stopping a pattern after one go; treating a jumbled row as a pattern; and with AAB, putting the single item after one A instead of two. Be careful with all-one-colour rows. Red, red, red does repeat, but it is not a good first example, because you cannot see where one part ends. Use two clear kinds first, and point to each unit as you say it.

In the lab your child drags the bead that comes next into the gap, copies a model row bead by bead, carries on a clap and stamp pattern, finds the one bead that breaks a pattern, and builds a two or three bead part that the pattern machine repeats three times. Each bead has its own shape mark as well as a colour.

familyTip: Make a pattern with things from the kitchen: spoon, cup, spoon, cup. Say it together, then ask 'What comes next?' Later, make one mistake on purpose and see if your child can find it.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: keep a bead pattern going, copy a row, clap and stamp, fix the bead that breaks it, and make your own pattern.

practice.prompt: Copying and making patterns: red, blue, red, blue, red… What comes next?
practice.hint: Say it out loud from the start. Which colour comes after red each time?
practice.explain: Red, blue is the part that repeats. After red comes blue, so the next bead is blue.

practice.prompt: Clap, stamp is the part that repeats. You do clap, stamp {n} times. How many claps is that?
practice.hint: Each clap, stamp part has one clap. Count the parts.
practice.explain: One clap in each part, and {n} parts, makes {n} claps. There are {n} stamps too.

practice.prompt: Car, car, bus, car, car, bus, car… What comes next?
practice.hint: Car, car, bus is the part that repeats. How many cars come before each bus?
practice.explain: Two cars come before every bus. Only one car has come so far, so the next one is a car.

practice.prompt: A bead string goes red, blue, red, blue. It has {n} red beads and ends with a blue one. How many beads is that in all?
practice.hint: Every red bead has a blue bead after it. Count the reds, then the blues.
practice.explain: {n} red beads and {n} blue beads make {=2*n} beads in all.

pool.prompt: Which row is a repeating pattern?
pool.hint: Look for a part that comes back again and again, in the same order.
pool.explain: Leaf, stick comes again in the same order, so it is a pattern. The other rows are mixed up.

pool.prompt: Clap, stamp, clap, stamp, clap… What comes next?
pool.hint: Say it with a beat: clap, stamp. What always comes after a clap?
pool.explain: Clap, stamp is the part that repeats, so after a clap comes a stamp.

pool.prompt: Car, car, bus is the part that repeats. You make it {n} times. How many buses is that?
pool.hint: Each car, car, bus part has one bus.
pool.explain: One bus in each part, made {n} times, gives {n} buses.

pool.prompt: Red, blue, red, red, red, blue. Which bead is wrong?
pool.hint: Say it from the start: red, blue, red… what should come 4th?
pool.explain: Red, blue, red, blue is the pattern. The 4th bead is red, but it should be blue.

pool.prompt: The top row is yellow, green, yellow, green. You copy it. What goes first in your row?
pool.hint: A copy starts the same way as the top row. Look at the first bead.
pool.explain: The top row starts with yellow, so your copy starts with yellow too, then green.

pool.prompt: Car, car, bus is the part that repeats. You make it {n} times. How many cars is that?
pool.hint: Each part has two cars. Count two cars for each part.
pool.explain: Two cars in each part, made {n} times, gives {=2*n} cars.

pool.prompt: You want to make your own pattern. Which is best to start?
choices: Pick red, yellow, then do it again and again
pool.hint: A pattern needs a part that repeats.
pool.explain: Pick a part, like red, yellow, and repeat it: red, yellow, red, yellow. That makes a pattern.

pool.prompt: Spoon, cup, cup, spoon, cup, cup, spoon… What comes next?
pool.hint: Spoon, cup, cup is the part. What comes after a spoon?
pool.explain: After each spoon come two cups. So after this spoon, the next one is a cup.
